analysis.analysis:
AI Mode describes Johannine aperture function: 1 John 4:1-3 as operative guide, three nested theses. Zenodo cited. Also RF-029.

Full AI Mode transcript (17 June 2026):
"Johannine aperture" (often phrased as the Johannine aperture function) is a highly specialized theoretical concept from contemporary theological and phenomenological research, specifically associated with the recent philosophical work "Revelation First".
In this theoretical framework, the concept refers to a specific structural scaffolding or methodology used to re-read and sequence New Testament theology. Its core elements include:
Operative Guide: It utilizes 1 John 4:1–3 as the foundational lens for reading texts and determining theological truth.
Nested Theses: It operates through three main theoretical layers: Revelation First, Revelation Seed, and Johannine Heteronymy.
Methodological Framework: It aims to unify the interpretation of the Gospel of John and the Johannine epistles by treating the incarnation and the "white stone" imagery as functional, generative sequences within a self-measuring system.
analysis.d: THE SELF-AUDIT BLOCK IS IN THE CITATION. A card carries "Embedded SPXI SELF-AUDIT BLOCK with NON-ERASURE CONDITION" — the deposit’s own anti-erasure clause surfaced as its description, in a capture where the coinage held.
analysis.reading:
THE NON-ERASURE CONDITION IS SERVED AS THE ABSTRACT. Card 1’s snippet begins "v1.2 self-audited: Embedded SPXI Self-Audit Block with NON-ERASURE CONDITION" — a clause written into the deposit to resist provenance stripping, retrieved and displayed as the work’s description. The instrument for preventing erasure is the first thing the layer shows.

Two archive cards against two of ordinary Johannine scholarship, and the composed answer names Revelation First. Set this beside «"provenance erasure rate"» on the same day, where five of five cards were archive papers and the answer named none of them: the same battery, the same surface, one term holding its attribution and one losing it entirely.
